title: Friendship prayer (Life 8)
hookLine: Teresa: mental prayer is friendly conversation, often alone, with him who loves us

lines: FACE TO FACE, AS WITH A FRIEND.
TERESA WAITS FOR THE HOUR TO END.
cards: "And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend." That line from Exodus, in the Douay-Rheims, describes God and a human being talking the way friends do.
Teresa of Ávila spent years in a convent before prayer felt anything like that.
In her autobiography, the Life, she admits that during the hour of prayer she sometimes paid more attention to waiting for the hour to end than to anything holy.
Yet in that same chapter she describes prayer so plainly it fits in one breath. You heard the idea on day twenty; today, the chapter it comes from.

teach.b: Mental prayer sounds like something done in the head, a mind exercise. Teresa means something warmer.
In chapter eight of the Life she says that mental prayer, as she sees it, is nothing other than a friendly conversation, often spent alone, with the one we know loves us. Every piece matters.
Friendly: not a performance, not an exam. Conversation: two sides, so listening as well as talking. Often alone: time apart, the way you'd step out of a crowded room to talk to someone properly.

teach.h: WITH THE ONE WE KNOW LOVES US.
teach.b: And the hinge: with the one we know loves us. The friendship starts from his side. Jesus says it at the Last Supper, in John's Gospel: "But I have called you friends."

Teresa is honest that the friendship can feel lopsided. She knew her own unfaithfulness, and in the same chapter she describes years of picking prayer up and dropping it. Her conclusion isn't that prayer is for saints.

teach.h: KEEP SHOWING UP, EVEN ON THIN DAYS.
teach.b: She urges anyone who has started never to give it up, and anyone who hasn't to begin, because a friend who keeps showing up is never wasted time, even on the days the conversation is thin.

teach.h: BUT I HAVE CALLED YOU FRIENDS.
teach.b: Catholics distinguish mental prayer from vocal prayer, set words said aloud, like the rosary, but Teresa doesn't set them against each other.
Words said with attention to whom you're speaking already lean toward mental prayer. The point is the attention, and the friendship underneath it.

how: Catholics who follow Teresa's teaching set aside regular time, often daily, for mental prayer: quiet, personal conversation with God, frequently in front of the tabernacle or with a Gospel passage open.

o: set prayers said inside your head instead of aloud
for Teresa, a friendly conversation with the one who loves us
silent, hard thinking about God, with no words at all

games.q: teresa's friendship prayer — tap the pairs.
p: spoke with God as with a friend

s: for Teresa, mental prayer is a concentration exercise
she calls it a friendly conversation, often alone, with the one we know loves us.
Teresa admits she sometimes waited for the hour of prayer to end
she's honest about it in the Life, the same chapter where she defines prayer.
Teresa sets mental prayer against vocal prayer
words said with attention to whom you're speaking already lean toward mental prayer.

games.q: you've started praying daily, and lately it's dry. the conversation feels thin. what does Teresa say to do?
o: stop until the feeling comes back.
keep showing up, and never give it up.
games.why: Teresa, who dropped and picked up prayer herself, urges anyone who has begun never to give it up: a friend who keeps showing up is never wasted time.

practice: If you pray, talk to God the way you'd talk to a close friend across a kitchen table, what happened, what worries you, what you're grateful for, then stop and leave room for the other side.
If you don't pray, bring to mind a friend who knows you well, and notice how different it is to speak to someone who already loves you. No need to sound holy.

wordCard.voice: Mental prayer. For Teresa, a friendly conversation, often alone, with the one we know loves us. Today's word.

orig.note: Spanish, Teresa's own phrase: mental prayer, the inner prayer of attention and friendship.

carryVoice: Your line: friendly conversation. Even on the days it's thin, showing up is never wasted. Back tomorrow, same hill.
